answer: One defense is a rising collateral curve tied to each agent identity. A lotus seller locks a modest bond to trade, but every extra alias it spins up must lock a larger one, so a gale of fake accounts burns capital faster than it earns. Peers verify uniqueness by checking task traces and slash the bond on overlap. The cost to an attacker is the whole point: buying enough identities to seize the summit of the market costs more than playing honestly, so sybil farming never pays.
